decision: Posted a regular user's delete for another user's note on the running app
why: The ticket says to stop if this does not happen on main. The delete action on origin/main is the same text as the commit that dropped the owner check.
result: 302 and the note is gone. The page has no Delete control. An admin with only delete:note:any gets 403.

decision: Ran the note-delete permission checker before changing the action
why: The checker compares the action with the notes page for every permission set. A failure here is the same bug, counted.

decision: Added the delete tests and ran them before changing the action
why: The failing test has to land while the bug is still present. Existing tests were left alone because they already cover the owner clicking Delete.
result: 2 failed, 1 passed. Stranger gets 302 and the note is gone. Admin gets 403. Owner still deletes.

decision: Restored the owner check in the note delete action
why: The action deleted by id after asking only for delete:note:own. The notes page already picks delete:note:own for the owner and delete:note:any for anyone else. The smallest fix is that same choice in the action.
result: tests pass, see the next rows

decision: Re-ran the delete tests after the action change
why: The same three tests that failed on main have to pass on the branch.

decision: Posted the same four deletes to the running app after the action change
why: The ticket is about the request, not only the test. A regular user's delete of someone else's note must be rejected and the note must remain.
result: stranger 403 and note remains. Owner 302 and note gone. Admin 302 and note gone.

decision: Updated the note-delete checker after the action changed shape
why: The old checker exited 2 because it still described an action that never reads ownerId. The new checker reads the ownership expression from the action and compares that choice with the notes page. The promise did not change.

decision: Re-ran the updated checker, then swapped the permission branches and restored them
why: A pass is not enough if the checker can no longer fail. Swapping own and any must still be a mismatch. Removing the ownership expression must exit 2. The action file was restored from git after both breaks.
result: exit 0 and 0 mismatches. Swapped branches exit 1 with 65536 mismatches. Hard-coded delete:note:own exits 2. Restored action exits 0.

decision: Moved the branch onto origin/main after the HTTP repro
why: Local main was 1c2c3b1 when the delete was reproduced. origin/main had moved to e510d0a. The note action file was unchanged, so the repro still applies. The failing test was re-run on that base before the first commit.
result: note action diff empty, tests still 2 failed and 1 passed

decision: Re-ran the whole unit suite after the fix
why: The first full run failed one GitHub callback test with a foreign key error. That file does not touch notes. Alone it passed, and the next full run passed.

decision: Supersedes the start-phase row. The retarget onto origin/main is a branch decision, not a new run.
why: That row used the start phase, which is reserved for a later run joining an existing log. The decision itself stands. The note action did not change between the repro commit and origin/main.

decision: Supersedes the full-suite row whose evidence was only on this machine.
why: A reviewer cannot open /tmp/vitest-all-2.txt. The same output is now in the repo.

decision: Supersedes the retarget row with a file that shows the note action did not change on origin/main
why: The HTTP repro and the failing test ran against that action text. origin/main moved, and the action file was identical, so the repro was not repeated on a second server.

decision: Supersedes the checker row. The swapped run and the hard-coded run are both in the repo.
why: The earlier row named only the passing checker file. The swap exits 1. Hard-coding delete:note:own exits 2. The action was restored and the passing run is check-branch.txt.
result: swap exit 1. hard-coded exit 2 is docs/note-delete-authorization/check-hardcoded.txt. restored pass is check-branch.txt

decision: Left the missing-note 404 where it already was
why: A logged-in delete of an unknown note id is 404 before the permission check. That order was already in the action. The ticket does not ask to hide whether a note id exists. An anonymous caller still hits requireUserId first.
